solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Realised what could be said of Scotland — but not home town (11)

indicatorNotes.but not: 'but not' excludes what follows, so those letters are taken away from the phrase before it

blocks.clueFragment: what could be said of Scotland
blocks.note: 'capital is Edinburgh', a true statement about Scotland
a burgh is a Scottish town

annotation.surface: Someone has a sudden realisation about Scotland, with a grudge against one particular town.
annotation.walkthrough: The Scottish fact is spelled out in full, then IN and BURGH are struck from the end of EDINBURGH to leave CAPITAL IS ED.
annotation.definitionFit: In finance, to realise an asset is to convert it to cash, a sense 'capitalised' shares; the surface wants the 'understood' sense instead.

entries.clue: Fruit nipper peeled, marked with spots (4,5)

indicatorNotes.peeled: a peeled word loses its outer skin, its first and last letters

blocks.note: a crab nips with its claws
DAPPLED with its outer D and D removed

annotation.surface: A child, peeled and spotty, seems to be the fruit of someone's loins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nipper' wants to be a small child; here it is the creature with pincers.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the crab apple is a small, sour wild apple.

entries.clue: What gets one over uninspiring Atlantic voyage? (10,8)

annotation.surface: A question about what makes a dull ocean voyage worth it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gets one over' sounds like getting the better of someone; it means literally helping a walker over the road.
annotation.definitionFit: A zebra or pelican marking gets a walker safely over the road, taking 'over' literally.

entries.clue: Time two notes to be played together (5)

blocks.note: UT (the old name for DO) and TI, from the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A conductor asks two notes to sound in time together.
annotation.walkthrough: UT is the old name for the first note of the scale, now usually called DO.
annotation.definitionFit: Italian for 'all', written in a score where every performer joins in.

entries.clue: Polygraph machine — electrode’s involved with it (3,8)

indicatorNotes.involved: involved can mean tangled up, and tangled letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A description of a polygraph: an electrode is part of the kit.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a true description, so the anagram hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the polygraph records pulse and sweating in the hope of catching untruths.

entries.clue: It seemed about the season to plant corn? (8)

indicatorNotes.about: about can mean turned around or scattered about, so the letters are moved into a new order

annotation.surface: A farmer's hunch that it was about time to sow the crop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'approximately' but tells you to rearrange IT SEEMED.
annotation.definitionFit: An old farming word, the time of year when seed goes into the ground, as in 'seedtime and harvest'.

entries.clue: Coat put on essential lifting device taking little energy and time (6,6)

blocks.note: to don = to put on clothing

annotation.surface: Instructions for putting a coat on, with a jack involved somehow.
annotation.walkthrough: A donkey jacket is a thick, short, dark British work coat with a leather or plastic panel across the shoulders.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the heavy British workman's jacket, typically with a shoulder panel.

entries.clue: Doing fair by niece, one who will gain from will? (11)

annotation.definition: one who will gain from will

indicatorNotes.Doing: to do something over is to rework it, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An uncle drawing up a will wants to do right by his niece.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly about a will, and the niece is the likely heir, so the answer sits right in the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: The legal term for whoever is left money or property in a will; the two senses of 'will' make the definition play.

entries.clue: Hungarian composer‘s band accepting a piece of music very well (4,6)

indicatorNotes.accepting: the band takes the next pieces inside it, as a host accepts guests

blocks.note: a bar of music, also inside BELT

annotation.surface: A band agrees to play a Hungarian composer's piece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a musical group, fitting the composer, but it is a strap.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Bartók (1881–1945) collected Hungarian folk songs and wrote the Concerto for Orchestra.

entries.clue: What’s black chess piece (not king) (5)

indicatorNotes.not: 'not king' means the piece without its K

blocks.note: a knight is a chess piece

annotation.surface: A chess question: which black piece is not the king?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Black' belongs with the chess pieces in the surface, but it goes with 'What's' to make the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose, cryptic definition: the dark hours are proverbially black, as in 'black as night'.

entries.clue: Handle issue in characteristic style (11)

blocks.note: to finger something is to handle it

annotation.surface: Advice to handle a matter with one's usual flair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Handle' reads as dealing with a problem; it is touching, which fits the answer neatly.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a distinctive mark by which someone's work can be identified, as in 'his fingerprints are all over it'.

entries.clue: Track events repeated regularly and aptly hard (5,4)

blocks.note: a cycle is a series of events that recurs
pat = aptly, as in a pat answer

annotation.surface: Athletics meetings held at intervals on a fittingly tough running track.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Track events' suggests athletics; 'Track' is the definition, and 'events repeated regularly' clues CYCLE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a lane or track set aside for bicycles.

entries.clue: Assistant dropping unknown from lead of Mozart opera (4)

indicatorNotes.dropping: tells you to let a letter fall away
indicatorNotes.lead of: the letter goes from the front of the word, its lead

blocks.note: Zaide, an unfinished opera by Mozart
Z, an algebraic unknown like X and Y

annotation.surface: An assistant is cut from the opening number of a Mozart opera.
annotation.walkthrough: Zaide is one of Mozart's lesser-known operas; take Z from its front.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, borrowed from French: an aide helps a senior figure, as in aide-de-camp.

entries.clue: I agree about large dog’s cry of pain (4)

indicatorNotes.about: about = around, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing sizes

annotation.surface: Someone agrees that the big dog is crying out in pain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large dog' reads as one idea, but 'large' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the short, sharp, high sound a hurt dog makes.

entries.clue: Check uranium found in part of mine (5)

indicatorNotes.found in: what is found in something sits inside it

blocks.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance passage into a mine
U, the chemical symbol for uranium

annotation.surface: A mine inspector checks for uranium in one of the tunnels.
annotation.walkthrough: ADIT is a crossword regular worth learning: a horizontal mine passage.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an audit is an official check, usually of accounts.

entries.clue: Persistent white tern always is around (7)

indicatorNotes.is around: the answer is around, present in the words just given

blocks.note: the answer runs from the last letter of 'white' through 'tern' into the start of 'always'

annotation.surface: A white tern is always hanging about.
annotation.walkthrough: The bird is real, which makes it hard to see TERN as the middle of the hidden answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: eternal complaints are persistent ones that never seem to stop.

entries.clue: Boy I trick, say, over ending a race (9)

indicatorNotes.over: over = turned over, so the string is reversed

annotation.surface: A boy confesses to a trick that brought a race to its end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ending a race' suggests the finish line of a sporting event; the race here is a people.
annotation.definitionFit: Genocide destroys a whole race or people, so genocidal describes what ends one.

entries.clue: Away without money and not inclined to drink (9)

indicatorNotes.without: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: tin is old slang for money

annotation.surface: Someone skint and off the booze stays away from the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without money' reads as broke; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the money goes inside rather than missing.
annotation.definitionFit: An abstinent person refrains from something, most often alcohol.

entries.clue: Disillusioned with meter debit out of control (10)

indicatorNotes.out of control: letters out of control run wild and end up in a new order

annotation.surface: A householder is soured by a meter running up a debt out of control.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a believable grumble about an energy bill, which hides the anagram well.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: someone embittered has lost their illusions and resents it.

entries.clue: Enticing green genie to work life-altering change (7,11)

indicatorNotes.to work: the letters are put to work, worked into a new shape

annotation.surface: A tempting green genie is put to work to change someone's life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Life-altering' sounds like a big personal event; read literally, it is altering living things.
annotation.definitionFit: Genetic engineering alters the DNA of living organisms, literally changing life.

entries.clue: Most noble of connections garnered by elite regularly (8)

indicatorNotes.garnered by: what is garnered is gathered in, so it goes inside
indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals, here every second one

annotation.surface: An elite gathers in its noblest connections.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Most noble of connections' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'noble'.
annotation.definitionFit: Lofty means exalted or noble in character, so the loftiest is the most noble.

entries.clue: Invention of a cold snack (4,3)

blocks.note: an invention is a made-up story, a lie; Cockney rhyming slang swaps 'lie' for a snack that rhymes with it
a British pastry-cased meat pie usually eaten cold

annotation.surface: Someone claims credit for inventing a cold snack.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang turns 'lie' into 'pork pie', often shortened to 'porky'. A pork pie is a British cold pastry pie filled with pork.
annotation.definitionFit: An invention can be a fabrication, a lie, which rhyming slang calls a pork pie; the snack sense is literal.

entries.clue: Birds in City of London street (7)

blocks.note: domestic fowl kept for eggs and meat
a street in the City near Bank station, named after the medieval bird market held there

annotation.surface: Birds are spotted in a street of London's financial district.
annotation.walkthrough: The City of London is the old financial square mile; Poultry is one of its streets, named for the medieval bird market there.
annotation.definitionFit: Poultry is domestic birds kept for eggs and meat, and also the name of a real City street.

entries.clue: American specialised soldier regularly leads (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals, here the 2nd and 4th

annotation.surface: An American special-forces soldier regularly takes the lead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American specialised soldier' reads as a single military unit; 'American specialised' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: At a US college, to major in a subject is to specialise in it; 'American' flags the usage.

entries.clue: Exhausted and wiped out, broken by pressure (8)

indicatorNotes.broken by: a word broken by a letter is split open with the letter inside

annotation.surface: Someone is exhausted, wiped out and cracking under pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one tired person, and 'wiped out' looks like a second definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: exhausted supplies are depleted, used up.

entries.clue: Ineffective medicine‘s rank smell (7)

blocks.note: a rank or position, a place

annotation.surface: A medicine that does nothing but smell foul.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rank' wants to be an adjective for the smell; it is a noun, a position.
annotation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active ingredient, used as a control in drug trials.

entries.clue: Assess girl with stringed instrument keeping in key (8)

indicatorNotes.keeping in: the instrument keeps the next letter inside it

annotation.surface: Judging a girl who plays the lute in tune.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' fits the musical surface; it is simply A, one of the keys.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to evaluate is to weigh up or assess something's worth.

entries.clue: Feat of splashing cash with compliment (14)

indicatorNotes.splashing: splashed letters scatter and land in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone manages to throw money about and flatter people at once.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Splashing cash' is a set phrase for spending freely, which disguises 'splashing' as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a feat is something achieved, an accomplishment.

entries.clue: Good ancient arable land fine for valuable cover (4,4)

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word

annotation.surface: Old farmland in good condition would fetch a fine price.
annotation.walkthrough: LEA is a crossword staple for a field.
annotation.definitionFit: Gold beaten wafer-thin and laid over a surface is a precious covering.

entries.clue: Old piece of key found in Tube (5)

indicatorNotes.found in: what is found in something sits inside it

annotation.surface: Part of a key is discovered on the London Underground.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'Tube' look like the London Underground; it is only a pipe. 'Old piece' is a coin, not a fragment.
annotation.definitionFit: A piece can be a coin, as in 'piece of eight'; the ducat was an old European gold coin.

entries.clue: One who works hard to reveal remains of cairn? (8)

blocks.note: British slang for someone given all the menial jobs
a cairn is a breed of small Scottish terrier, so its remains would be a canine corpse

annotation.surface: An archaeologist digs hard to uncover what lies under a pile of stones.
annotation.walkthrough: A cairn looks like a heap of stones marking a grave, which fits 'remains'; here it is a small Scottish terrier. The question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Dogsbody is British slang for someone given all the menial jobs, and read literally it is the body of a dog.

entries.clue: Did revolt spread beyond port? (6)

indicatorNotes.beyond: what is beyond comes after, so TED follows RIO

blocks.note: to ted is to spread out mown grass to dry

annotation.surface: A question: did a rebellion spread past the harbour?
annotation.walkthrough: TED is an old farming verb, spreading hay to dry, and a crossword favourite.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the past tense: to riot is to revolt violently.

entries.clue: Toothpaste certified prepared without nitrogen (10)

indicatorNotes.prepared: prepared means made up, so the letters are made into a new word
indicatorNotes.without: without in the old sense of outside: the prepared letters sit around the N

blocks.note: N, the chemical symbol for nitrogen, added to the mix

annotation.surface: A toothpaste is certified to be made without nitrogen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without nitrogen' looks like a product claim, as if the paste lacked it; in fact N is added, sitting inside the rearranged letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Dentifrice is the formal word for any paste or powder for cleaning teeth.

entries.clue: What helps one see travelling dandy going round well-dressed (3,4)

indicatorNotes.going round: the first word goes round the second

annotation.surface: A travelling dandy goes about town in his finery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Travelling' looks like it describes the dandy; it belongs to the definition, and 'dandy' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A fog lamp is a car light that helps a driver see on the road in fog.

entries.clue: Reportedly lamenting parrot eating grand Ipomoea (7,5)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: what is reported is heard, so take the sound rather than the spelling
indicatorNotes.eating: the parrot eats, taking G at its side here as a charade

blocks.note: a lory is a brightly coloured parrot

annotation.surface: A grieving parrot tucks into some expensive plant.
annotation.walkthrough: LORY is a crossword parrot worth knowing.
annotation.definitionFit: Ipomoea is the botanical genus of the morning glory, a twining plant whose flowers open in the morning.

entries.clue: I’m pleased nice hero is pious (5-5)

blocks.note: a goody is the good guy in a story

annotation.surface: Someone is delighted that a hero is a devout type.
annotation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: an exclamation, then a noun for the good guy.
annotation.definitionFit: Goody-goody is a disapproving word for someone smugly virtuous, a sanctimonious sense of pious.

entries.clue: Show Belgian port’s terminus perhaps exporting diamonds and sulphur (11)

indicatorNotes.exporting: exporting sends things out, so those letters leave

blocks.note: a terminus is an end-of-line station
S, the chemical symbol for sulphur

annotation.surface: A Belgian port station ships out diamonds and sulphur.
annotation.walkthrough: D leaves OSTEND and S leaves STATION, each one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: ostentation is showy display meant to impress.

entries.clue: At first believe old butcher’s lamb tender (2-4)

indicatorNotes.At first: take the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: butcher's hook is rhyming slang for look, a peep

annotation.surface: An old butcher swears his lamb is tender.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' means a look via Cockney rhyming slang (butcher's hook = look). 'Tender' is not soft but someone who tends.
annotation.definitionFit: Little Bo-Peep, of the nursery rhyme, is a shepherdess who lost her sheep, so she tends lambs.

entries.clue: Instrument‘s power level is over quiet (6,5)

indicatorNotes.is over: in a down clue, over means placed above, so P and LAYER come before PIANO

annotation.surface: An instrument's volume is turned right down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Power level' reads as volume; the words split into P and LAYER.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a pianola, a piano that plays itself from a perforated roll.

entries.clue: Visitor from east sheltering in wind (5)

indicatorNotes.sheltering in: the letter shelters inside the next word

annotation.surface: A traveller from the East shelters from the wind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Visitor from east' reads as a traveller; 'from' only links, and 'east' is E.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a guest is someone visiting.

entries.clue: Obtained work that is having reduced tax and lose it (2,2,6)

indicatorNotes.reduced: a reduced word is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: CESS, an old word for a tax, with its last S removed

annotation.surface: Someone earning after a tax cut still manages to lose their temper.
annotation.walkthrough: CESS is an archaic tax, now familiar from crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to lose it and to go to pieces both mean to lose control of oneself.

entries.clue: Where location of Portsmouth harbour entrance is irrelevant (6,3,5)

annotation.definition2: Where location of Portsmouth harbour entrance is

blocks.clueFragment: Where location of Portsmouth harbour entrance is
blocks.note: Portsmouth's harbour mouth lies by the Point, a spit of land in Old Portsmouth

annotation.surface: A remark that where Portsmouth's harbour entrance is does not matter.
annotation.walkthrough: Portsmouth is a naval port on England's south coast; the Point is a spit at the harbour mouth, so the entrance is literally beside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a remark beside the point has no bearing on the matter, while the harbour mouth literally sits by the Point.

entries.clue: Man Dr Dale treated for state of unconsciousness (9)

indicatorNotes.treated: treated letters are worked on, processed into a new order

annotation.surface: A patient is treated by a doctor for being unconscious.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface, with its doctor and treatment, makes 'treated' look literal.
annotation.definitionFit: Dreamland is a light, humorous name for sleep.

entries.clue: Diatribe‘s answer resounded in tone (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the pieces go in the next word

blocks.note: a hue is a tone of colour

annotation.surface: A rant's reply echoes in its tone of voice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tone' looks like tone of voice, which suits the rant; it is a colour, HUE.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a harangue is a long, forceful attacking speech.

entries.clue: Chosen Republican regularly teases voter (9)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals, here every second one

annotation.surface: A chosen Republican keeps teasing a voter.
annotation.walkthrough: An electress was the wife of a German prince-elector, or a woman with a vote.
annotation.definitionFit: An old word for a female elector, one who votes.

entries.clue: Hand in money in Brazil for pardoning (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the first word goes in the second

annotation.surface: Someone hands in cash in Brazil in exchange for a pardon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hand in' looks like a phrasal verb, submitting something; 'Hand' is MITT and 'in' is the container signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Remittal is the act of remitting, cancelling a debt or penalty, which is a pardoning.

entries.clue: One dug out new underground room (7)

indicatorNotes.out: letters knocked out of place are rearranged

blocks.note: N = new, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Someone digs out a new cellar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dug out' reads as a phrasal verb about excavating, fitting the cellar; 'out' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a prison cell underground, beneath a castle.

entries.clue: Movement that’s annoyed feral cat taking time out (7)

indicatorNotes.taking: the word takes away the next part
indicatorNotes.out: the removed letters are taken out

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

annotation.surface: An angry wild cat takes some time out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feral cat' reads as one animal, but the deletion works on 'feral' alone. OUNCE, the snow leopard, is a crossword favourite.
annotation.definitionFit: To flounce is to storm off with exaggerated movements, showing annoyance.

entries.clue: Wide area of plant endlessly filling river (7)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: without its end, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.filling: the plant fills the river, going inside it

blocks.note: the Exe, a river in Devon

annotation.surface: A plant spreads unchecked across a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The Exe is a crossword-favourite river in south-west England.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an expanse is a wide open stretch of land, sea or sky.

entries.clue: Banning or backing me visiting pubs? (10)

indicatorNotes.backing: backing means going backwards, so ME is reversed

annotation.surface: A choice between barring me and supporting my trips to the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banning or backing' looks like two opposite verbs; 'backing' is the reversal signal.
annotation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade, so embargoing is banning.

entries.clue: Ground corn‘s right stuffed into marrow (5)

indicatorNotes.stuffed into: one letter is stuffed into the word that follows

blocks.note: the marrow of an argument is its core, its gist

annotation.surface: A recipe: stuff a marrow with ground corn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marrow' looks like the vegetable, which suits the stuffing; it is the core of something.
annotation.definitionFit: Grist is grain for grinding or already ground, as in 'grist to the mill'.

entries.clue: I am receiving treatment for itching (9)

annotation.surface: A patient explains they are being treated for an itch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Itching' looks like the symptom being treated; it means restless, eager.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be itching to do something is to be restless and eager, unwilling to wait.

entries.clue: Trick’s beginning with bottom card of winning suit (5)

indicatorNotes.beginning: a word's beginning is its first letter, so only that is used

annotation.surface: A card player starts a trick with their lowest card from the winning suit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottom card' reads as the lowest card; 'bottom' is the backside.
annotation.definitionFit: A trump is any card of the suit that outranks the others for that hand.

entries.clue: Somewhat exotically having a shell-like nature? (4)

indicatorNotes.Somewhat: somewhat = part of, so only part of the next word is used

blocks.note: the answer sits inside the word, after its first two letters

annotation.surface: Something unusual has a nature like a seashell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shell-like' is British slang for an ear, as in 'a word in your shell-like'; it looks like seashells.
annotation.definitionFit: Otic means relating to the ear, and 'shell-like' is jokey slang for an ear.

entries.clue: Very large centre in Toulouse city (4)

indicatorNotes.centre in: take the middle letters of the word

blocks.note: the two middle letters of touLOuse

annotation.surface: A huge city centre in southern France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Toulouse city' reads as one place; the definition is 'city' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

entries.clue: Conductor‘s to study in Italy initially (9)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially = at the start, so only the word's opening letter is used

blocks.note: to scan is to study closely

annotation.surface: A conductor goes to study in Italy at the start of his career.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is plausible biography, since Toscanini was Italian.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral conductor.

entries.clue: Country road Tim found in car with never an end (7)

indicatorNotes.found in: what is found in something sits inside it
indicatorNotes.with never an end: none of the three words keeps its last letter

blocks.note: car without its end, holding ROA and TI

annotation.surface: Tim is found on a country road in a car that never stops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With never an end' applies to all three words, not only the car.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Croatia is a country on the Adriatic.

entries.clue: Without protection Zunis and Utes stick together (5)

indicatorNotes.Without protection: the outer letters protect a word; without them only the inside is left

blocks.note: Zunis without its outer Z and S
Utes without its outer U and S

annotation.surface: Two Native American peoples, left unprotected, band together.
annotation.walkthrough: The Zuni and Ute are Native American peoples of the south-western US; only their inner letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to unite is to join or stick together.

entries.clue: Harmonises decorations in a make-over (11)

indicatorNotes.in a make-over: letters given a make-over are remade in a new order

annotation.surface: An interior designer matches up the ornaments during a makeover.
annotation.walkthrough: The makeover surface fits the answer's colour-matching sense, so the anagram sits in its own scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: coordinating colours or parts makes them harmonise.

entries.clue: Business listing has unnerved hotel workers (6,5)

annotation.surface: A trade directory reports that hotel staff are rattled.
annotation.walkthrough: Pages are young hotel staff who carry messages and call guests' names.
annotation.definitionFit: The Yellow Pages is a printed telephone directory of businesses, arranged by trade.
